## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(ggVennDiagram)
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
chlor <- read.csv("rfp_chlor.csv")
sym <- read.csv("rfp_table_sym.csv")
phen <- read.csv("sig_feat_phenotype_rfpermute.csv")
dep <- read.csv("sig_feat_dep_rfpermute.csv")
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
chlor_sig <- chlor |> filter(`X.IncMSE.pval` < 0.05)
  
sym_sig <- sym |> filter(`X.IncMSE.pval` < 0.05)
```

```{r}

venn_data <- list(
  Chlor = chlor_sig$Feature,
  Sym = sym_sig$Feature,
  Phen = phen$Feature,
  Dep = dep$Feature
)
```

```{r}

venn_obj <- Venn(venn_data)
venn <- ggVennDiagram(venn_data, label_color = "white")

venn
```

```{r}
overlap(venn_obj)
```
